title: 📘 UNIT 5: GLOBAL AND REGIONAL DEVELOPMENTS SINCE 1945
notes:
🌍 After World War II, the world experienced major political, economic and social changes.

 The United Nations was established, the USA and USSR emerged as superpowers, the Cold War divided the world, Asian countries experienced wars and revolutions, newly independent states formed the Non-Aligned Movement, Arab-Israeli conflicts continued, and the Soviet Union eventually collapsed.

title: 5.1 🇺🇳 THE UNITED NATIONS ORGANIZATION
notes:
🇺🇳 The United Nations was established in 1945 to maintain international peace, prevent future wars and promote cooperation among nations.

📅 Important steps in its formation:
• August 1941, Atlantic Charter by Franklin D. Roosevelt and Winston Churchill.
• January 1942, Declaration by the United Nations was signed by 26 countries.
• 1943, Moscow and Tehran Conferences supported the idea of a world organization.
• 1944, Dumbarton Oaks Conference prepared proposals for the organization.
• June 26, 1945, 50 countries signed the UN Charter at San Francisco.
• October 24, 1945, the United Nations officially came into existence.

title: 5.1.1 🎯 MISSION AND PRINCIPLES OF THE UN
notes:
🎯 Main purposes:
• Maintain international peace and security.
• Promote friendly relations among nations.
• Encourage international economic, social and humanitarian cooperation.
• Promote human rights and fundamental freedoms.
• Settle international disputes peacefully.

📜 Major principles → sovereign equality of states, peaceful settlement of disputes, respect for territorial integrity, political independence and non-interference in domestic affairs.

title: 5.1.2 🏛️ SIX PRINCIPAL ORGANS
notes:
🏛️ General Assembly → includes all member states and discusses international issues.

🛡️ Security Council → responsible mainly for international peace and security. Its five permanent members have veto power.

👤 Secretariat → carries out the daily work of the UN under the Secretary-General.

⚖️ International Court of Justice → settles legal disputes between states.

💰 Economic and Social Council → coordinates international economic and social activities.

🤝 Trusteeship Council → supervised trust territories and helped prepare them for self-government or independence.

title: 5.1.3 🏆 UN ACHIEVEMENTS AND CHALLENGES
notes:
🏆 Achievements → peacekeeping, humanitarian assistance, promotion of human rights, support for decolonization, international cooperation and development.

📜 1948 → Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted.

⚠️ Challenges → conflicts among powerful states, use of the Security Council veto, limited resources and difficulties in stopping some wars.

⭐ Overall → the UN became the major international organization for peace and cooperation.

title: 5.2 🧊 RISE OF THE SUPERPOWERS AND BEGINNING OF THE COLD WAR
notes:
🌍 World War II weakened the traditional European powers and left two dominant superpowers: the United States and Soviet Union.

🇺🇸 USA → supported capitalism, liberal democracy and a market economy.

☭ USSR → supported communism, one-party rule and a centrally planned economy.

⚔️ Post-war tensions → disagreement over Eastern Europe, Germany, political systems and economic influence increased hostility.

🧊 Cold War → prolonged political, ideological, economic and military rivalry between the USA and USSR without direct full-scale war between them.

🌎 Result → the world became largely divided into a Western bloc led by the USA and an Eastern bloc led by the USSR.

title: 5.2.1 🛡️ COLD WAR STRATEGIES
notes:
🇺🇸 Truman Doctrine, 1947 → the USA promised assistance to countries threatened by communism, especially Greece and Turkey.

💰 Marshall Plan → American economic assistance helped rebuild Western Europe and strengthen resistance to communism.

☭ Molotov Plan → Soviet economic assistance supported Eastern European countries aligned with the USSR.

🛡️ Containment → strategy associated with George Kennan that aimed to stop the expansion of communism.

🌍 Military alliances → NATO was formed in 1949, while the Warsaw Pact was formed in 1955.

title: 5.2.2 ☢️ ARMS RACE
notes:
☢️ Arms Race → the USA and USSR competed to develop increasingly powerful nuclear and conventional weapons.

📅 1945 → atomic bombs were used against Hiroshima and Nagasaki.
📅 1949 → USSR developed its atomic bomb.
📅 1952 → USA tested the hydrogen bomb.
📅 1953 → USSR developed the hydrogen bomb.
📅 1957 → USSR launched Sputnik, the first artificial Earth satellite.

⚠️ Effects → increased fear of nuclear war, consumed huge resources, intensified rivalry and placed economic pressure on both superpowers.

title: 5.3 🌏 ASIA DURING THE COLD WAR
notes: 🌏 Asia became a major area of Cold War rivalry. Japan experienced rapid post-war recovery, Korea was divided and fought a war, China underwent a communist revolution, and Vietnam became the center of a major anti-communist conflict.

title: 5.3.1 🇯🇵 JAPAN AFTER WORLD WAR II
notes:
🇯🇵 Japan was severely damaged by World War II but recovered rapidly.

🇺🇸 US influence → Japan became a close American ally as the Cold War intensified.

🏭 Economic recovery → American assistance and industrial development helped rebuild Japan.

📜 1947 Constitution → established democratic institutions and renounced war as a means of national policy.

⭐ Result → Japan became a major industrial and economic power in Asia.

title: 5.3.2 🇰🇷 KOREAN WAR, 1950–1953
notes:
🇰🇷 Korea had been under Japanese rule until 1945 and was later divided along the 38th parallel.

🇰🇵 North Korea → communist government led by Kim Il Sung.
🇰🇷 South Korea → anti-communist government led by Syngman Rhee.

📅 June 1950 → North Korea invaded South Korea.

🇺🇳 UN forces and the USA supported South Korea, while China entered the war in support of North Korea.

📅 1953 → Armistice signed at Panmunjom.

📌 Result → Korea remained divided into North Korea and South Korea.

title: 5.3.3 🇨🇳 CHINESE REVOLUTION
notes:
🇨🇳 Chinese Civil War → developed mainly between the Chinese Communist Party and the Nationalist Party.

👤 Mao Zedong → leader of the Chinese Communist Party.
👤 Chiang Kai-shek → leader of the Nationalists.

📅 1949 → Mao's communists won and established the People's Republic of China.

🇹🇼 Chiang Kai-shek and Nationalist forces withdrew to Taiwan.

🌍 Cold War effect → communist victory strengthened the communist bloc in Asia and increased American concern about the spread of communism.

title: 5.3.4 🇻🇳 VIETNAM WAR
notes:
🇻🇳 After the First Indochina War, Vietnam was divided between communist North Vietnam and non-communist South Vietnam.

👤 Ho Chi Minh → leader of North Vietnam and the Vietnamese communist movement.

🇺🇸 USA → supported South Vietnam to prevent communist expansion.
☭ USSR and China → supported North Vietnam.

📅 1960 → Viet Cong, also called the National Liberation Front, emerged in South Vietnam.
📅 1965 → President Johnson intensified American bombing of North Vietnam.
📅 January 27, 1973 → peace agreement was signed and US involvement ended.
📅 1975 → North Vietnam defeated South Vietnam and reunified the country.
📅 July 2, 1976 → Socialist Republic of Vietnam was formally established.

title: 5.4 🌍 NON-ALIGNED MOVEMENT
notes:
🌍 Non-Aligned Movement, or NAM → movement of countries that sought to remain independent from the major Cold War blocs.

📅 April 18–24, 1955 → Bandung Conference in Indonesia brought together 29 Asian and African leaders.

📅 September 1961 → first NAM Conference was held in Belgrade, Yugoslavia.

👥 Important leaders → Josip Broz Tito, Gamal Abdel Nasser, Jawaharlal Nehru, Kwame Nkrumah and Sukarno.

🎯 Main purpose → protect national independence and sovereignty while opposing colonialism, imperialism, racism and foreign domination.

title: 5.4.1 🕊️ PRINCIPLES AND IMPORTANCE OF NAM
notes:
🕊️ Major principles → respect for sovereignty, territorial integrity, peaceful coexistence, non-interference, self-determination and opposition to colonialism and racism.

🌍 Importance → NAM gave newly independent countries a collective voice in world affairs.

💡 It also promoted economic cooperation, national independence, disarmament and opposition to great-power domination.

title: 5.5 🇮🇱 ARAB–ISRAELI CONFLICT
notes:
🌍 The Arab-Israeli conflict developed from competing Arab and Jewish national claims over Palestine.

📜 1917 → Balfour Declaration supported the establishment of a Jewish homeland in Palestine.

✡️ Zionism → Jewish nationalist movement that sought a Jewish homeland.

👤 Theodor Herzl → important founder of modern political Zionism.

📅 1947 → UN proposed partitioning Palestine into Jewish and Arab states, with Jerusalem internationalized.

📅 May 14, 1948 → Israel declared independence.

⚔️ May 15, 1948 → Egypt, Syria, Iraq and Trans-Jordan entered the war against Israel.

📌 Result → Israel survived and expanded its territory, while many Palestinians became refugees.

title: 5.5.1 ⚔️ MAJOR ARAB–ISRAELI WARS
notes:
⚔️ 1948 War → followed the creation of Israel and produced major territorial changes and Palestinian displacement.

🚢 Suez War, 1956 → followed Egypt's nationalization of the Suez Canal. Israel, Britain and France attacked Egypt, but international pressure forced them to withdraw.

⚔️ Six-Day War, 1967 → Israel fought Egypt, Syria and Jordan and gained control of the Golan Heights, Jerusalem, West Bank, Gaza Strip and Sinai.

⚔️ Yom Kippur War, 1973 → Egypt and Syria attacked Israel. The war increased international tensions and contributed to a major oil crisis.

🇵🇸 PLO → Palestinian Liberation Organization continued the Palestinian struggle under leaders including Yasser Arafat.

title: 5.6 ☭ COLLAPSE OF THE SOVIET UNION
notes:
☭ By the 1980s, the Soviet Union faced serious economic difficulties, political problems, growing nationalism and increasing demands for reform.

👤 Mikhail Gorbachev → became leader of the Soviet Communist Party in 1985 and introduced major reforms.

🗣️ Glasnost → greater openness, transparency, freedom of speech and freedom of the press.

🔄 Perestroika → restructuring of the Soviet political and economic system, including limited private economic activity.

📌 Effect → reforms encouraged demands for greater freedom and weakened communist political control.

title: 5.6.1 🧱 CHANGES IN EASTERN EUROPE
notes:
🌍 After World War II, several Central and Eastern European countries became Soviet satellite states.

📅 1989 → nationalist and democratic movements spread across Eastern Europe.

🇵🇱 Poland, Hungary, Czechoslovakia, Romania and other states experienced the collapse of communist governments.

🧱 Berlin Wall → fell on November 9, 1989, becoming a major symbol of the collapse of communist division in Europe.

📌 Result → Soviet influence in Eastern Europe declined rapidly and the Soviet Union itself became increasingly unstable.

title: 5.6.2 🏁 END OF THE SOVIET UNION
notes:
⚠️ Causes of collapse → economic weakness, political reforms, nationalist movements, loss of control over Eastern Europe and growing opposition to communist rule.

📅 1991 → an attempted coup against Gorbachev failed and further weakened the Soviet government.

📅 December 1991 → the Soviet Union was formally dissolved.

🇷🇺 Result → Russia became the main successor state and several Soviet republics became independent.

⭐ Significance → the collapse of the USSR marked the end of the Cold War and the bipolar world order.
